c.st: Just Got Out of Prison. Now What?
c.x:
Except that most people will be happy to pay the extra taxes if it makes the streets safer.

I think the best way to get serious reform is to point out the relationship between crime and punishment has gotten a bit too loose, and that it's a matter of basic justice to expect the punishment to fit the crime.

> There are far too many people who have no place in society and there is zero benefit to society to continue their existence.

This is not connected to crime and punishment in any way; merely not benefiting society in any way isn't a crime, let alone a capital one.

I can't say that I've researched the history of crime and punishment over the centuries and how imprisonment fits into that. Though I was intending to refer to more recent history, somewhere from around the founding of America to the beginning of modern-era widespread policing.
